title: Vacuum nanogap field-emission access device
idea: Replace the semiconductor channel with a ~10 nm vacuum gap between a sharpened storage-node tip and the bitline electrode, gated by the wordline (a vacuum tube fused into the cell). It conducts only by gate-assisted field emission.
why: No junction, BTBT or diffusion current exists in the off state, so leakage is near zero and the cell is radiation hard.

title: Coin-minting nanoimprint strikes the access-pillar layer instead of EUV
idea: Write one master die by e-beam, replicate working stamps, and strike the access-pillar layer by nanoimprint like coin minting. A reverse-tone, self-aligned spacer step reaches sub-12 nm pillars.
why: Fact 4: removes 1-2 EUV exposures from the access device module. Imprint's low line-edge roughness tightens VT spread and so trims the leakage tail.

title: Substitute periodic refresh with static Esaki tunnel-diode latch per cell
idea: Substitute capacitor decay plus refresh with a bistable hold: two series interband (Esaki) tunnel diodes at the storage node form a negative-differential-resistance latch with two stable voltages. A tiny valley current (target ~pA) holds the state continuously, and the access transistor still reads and writes it.
why: Removes refresh entirely (16-33% of idle power, 10-20% of bandwidth) in exchange for a static current; viable if the valley current is engineered below ~10 pA per cell.

title: Electrometer guard bootstrap shields the write transistor
idea: A 4T gain cell has two series write transistors. The source-follower read transistor drives their middle node to track the storage voltage, as a guarded electrometer input does, so the inner device sees Vds~0. This fits a 250-180 nm logic process.
why: Subthreshold current, proportional to 1-exp(-Vds/kT), falls ~100x, giving long retention without a special material.

title: Magnify leakage on purpose: canary cells set refresh pace
idea: Seed every subarray with replica canary cells built 5-10x leakier (shorter channel, deliberate defect implant) that are sensed cheaply on a slow timer; a subarray is refreshed only when its canaries decay. Refresh then tracks real temperature, voltage and aging instead of a worst-case 85 C spec.
why: Real leakage is usually 10-50x below worst case, so refresh energy and bandwidth drop ~10x on average.

title: Junctionless access nanowire: predictable decay for cold-boot-proof vaults
idea: Secure-key vaults want memory that decays on a known schedule, which needs a tight leakage distribution. Use a uniformly doped junctionless nanowire access device: with no metallurgical p-n junction there is no junction field peak or dopant-gradient trap zone, so the trap-assisted-tunneling outliers that form the leakage tail largely vanish.
why: Fact 3: refresh is set by the tail, not the median; compressing the tail toward the median could lengthen worst-case retention 5-10x, with a 'decays in N seconds' secure-memory product as a bonus.

title: Segmented gate: negative retention finger guards the storage junction
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation resolves 'strong on-current vs. tiny off-leakage': split the buried wordline into a long drive segment on the bitline side and a short, independently driven 'retention finger' over the storage-node junction. The finger sits at about -1 V except during the ~20 ns activation, so the drain field and trap-assisted tunnelling at the storage node are borne by a deeply-off segment while the drive segment can use a lower Vt.
why: Attacks Fact 3 (<=13 fA tail, GIDL/TAT dominated): target 10-50x lower tail leakage, stretching refresh from 32-64 ms toward ~1 s and recovering most of the 10-20% refresh bandwidth loss, at the cost of a second wordline driver per row.

title: Air gaps between buried wordlines stop passing-gate leakage
idea: Effect: fringing-field coupling (passing-gate effect). The oxide between neighbouring buried wordlines and the storage-node junction becomes a sealed air gap (k~1), so a neighbour's 3 V swing no longer lowers the barrier of the passing cell, removing the activity-dependent leakage spikes that force conservative refresh. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3) with row-hammer relief (fact 9): claims ~2x tail improvement; process drop-in.

title: Deuterium passivation targeted only at the storage-node junction
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: the leakage tail lives at the storage-node junction and its interface traps, so give that one spot a different material property. A self-aligned opening at the storage-node contact admits a deuterium implant plus anneal; Si-D bonds resist hot-carrier and thermal depassivation far better than Si-H (giant isotope effect), so tail traps stay passivated over life and VRT is suppressed.
why: Narrows the retention tail and variable-retention-time population (Fact 3); claim 2-4x longer worst-case retention using only an extra masked implant.

title: Western Electric relay contacts reborn as NEM access relays
idea: Revive the Bell System's palladium-contact telephone relays: each access device is a nanoelectromechanical relay with palladium/platinum contacts from Montana's Stillwater mines, built with the aluminum-hinge micromirror MEMS process already run at high volume in Texas, which shows >1e12 switching cycles. An open contact leaks nothing.
why: Zero off-state leakage (fact 3) so refresh vanishes, and galvanic isolation blocks row-hammer coupling (fact 9); built in U.S. MEMS fabs without EUV. Endurance toward 1e15 cycles is the main risk.

title: Image-sensor 4T pixel gain cell reads 1,000-electron packets
idea: Box: buried-channel storage well (~1-2k e-) x transfer gate + floating-diffusion source follower borrowed from 4T image pixels x correlated-double-sampling column sensing x planar CMOS x Si x CIS fab flow. Full charge transfer onto a tiny floating diffusion gives ~100 uV/e- gain, so a small well replaces the 5 fF capacitor and is written back after read.
why: Escapes the capacitor charge wall (fact 1); buried-channel wells with CIS-grade dark current (few e-/s) extend retention 10-100x (fact 3); reuses existing CIS fab capacity.

title: Global-shutter pinned storage node borrowed from image sensors
idea: Image sensors hold photo-charge in pinned memory nodes for hundreds of ms with dark current of a few electrons per second, by burying the n storage region under a p+ pinning layer that keeps it away from the Si/SiO2 interface. Build the DRAM storage-node junction as such a pinned structure so interface-state generation is screened off.
why: Fact 3: surface and junction generation leakage could drop >10x, leaving channel leakage, which Vt can fix; fitting the pinning layer into 6F^2 is the challenge.

title: Carbon-cluster proximity gettering borrowed from image-sensor dark current
idea: Effect: impurity gettering. C3H5 molecular-ion clusters implanted ~1 um below the array (the CMOS image-sensor technique that cut dark current) form a dense sink that traps Fe, Cu and Ni during thermal steps, pulling midgap metal generation centres away from storage junctions. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): 2-5x lower junction leakage tail, the same physics as CIS dark current; one substrate step.

title: Uncorrectable-error insurance underwrites relaxed-refresh deployments
idea: Operators won't run DRAM outside spec because a rare uncorrectable error is an unpriced tail risk. Form a small underwriting venture that prices that risk from controlled retention-stress data and fleet telemetry. It sells per-server policies that pay out on detected uncorrectable errors for customers running certified extended-refresh settings. The actuarial model, test lab and a reinsurer partnership fit within $1M and 24 months.
why: This turns a technical guardband (2-4x refresh margin) into a financial one, unlocking 2-4x refresh savings in fleets that would never adopt them unhedged (fact 3).

title: Five-star tube grading reborn: retention-graded DRAM for relaxed refresh
idea: Revive the military practice of hand-selecting premium 'five-star' vacuum tubes: test every U.S.-made DRAM die for retention on U.S. testers, bin the tail-free fraction as long-retention parts certified for a 4-8x refresh interval, and sell them at a premium to U.S. hyperscalers whose controllers apply the certified interval.
why: Monetizes the natural retention distribution (fact 3): 4-8x less refresh energy and bandwidth on graded parts with no process change, and a business case for domestic fabs.

title: Blood-clotting self-heal pulses seal leakage paths in the field
idea: Platelets clot only at the wound; put an oxygen-rich reservoir film (over-stoichiometric HfO2+x or CeO2) next to the access junction and gate dielectric, and when profiling flags a leaky cell, send a localized heal pulse whose Joule heat is confined to the conductive defect chain, driving oxygen from the reservoir to fill the vacancy cluster.
why: Gives a cell-local in-situ anneal while the chip stays below 400 C, removing variable-retention and tail cells after fabrication and during aging, so the array runs nearer median retention (10-100x the tail) with 5-10x less refresh.

title: Millefiori glass-cane draw sliced into litho-free vertical access arrays
idea: Assemble a cm-scale preform holding ~10^4 coaxial access-transistor cross-sections (chalcogenide-glass semiconductor core, glass gate dielectric, low-melting metal gate). Thermally draw it 10^4x as Venetian millefiori cane or optical fiber is drawn, then slice 100 nm discs: each slice is a ready-made array of vertical gate-all-around access switches.
why: Capital intensity and fact 4: removes the EUV patterning of the access layer altogether. A wide-gap glassy channel gives low off-current, and one draw tower replaces scanners for this layer.

title: Bit-plane layout: MSB planes refresh fast, LSB planes rarely
idea: Rearrange tensor layout: transpose AI weights and activations into bit-planes so each DRAM row holds one significance level, then give sign/MSB rows normal refresh and the lowest 3-4 bit-plane rows 8-16x slower refresh. Rare decay flips in LSB planes perturb values by less than quantization noise, which models already tolerate.
why: Refresh energy (fact 3) for AI memory drops ~40-50% (half the planes at 1/8 rate); needs only per-region refresh rates.

title: Compression pays for ECC: freed bits buy stronger codes
idea: 10-person constraint: controller logic only. Compress each 64 B line (base-delta or FP-exponent compression). When a line shrinks by at least 12.5%, store a stronger BCH or Reed-Solomon code in-line in the freed bits so the line can sit in a 4-8x slower refresh tier. Incompressible lines keep normal refresh.
why: Fact 3: with ~60-70% of AI and server lines compressible, most memory moves to a slow refresh tier at no capacity cost.

title: Laminate a hundred ultrathin glass memory sheets into a 3D block
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: instead of growing 26+ tiers monolithically, build one memory tier per 25-50 um flexible-glass sheet roll-to-roll, test every sheet, then nest 50-100 known-good sheets in a laminated stack with edge-plated wordline/bitline risers and a periphery chiplet at the edge.
why: Sidesteps the 3D DRAM tier-yield problem (Fact 2) with test-and-discard per tier; ultrathin glass is U.S.-made, and low-leakage TFTs let each tier refresh at ~1 Hz (Fact 3).

title: Eliminate deposited dielectrics: Bi2O2Se channel with native Bi2SeO5 gate oxide
idea: Grow 2D Bi2O2Se by CVD and partly convert it with UV-ozone or O2 plasma into its native high-k (k~20) Bi2SeO5, forming a Si/SiO2-like clean interface on an atomically thin body; the access device reaches near-60 mV/dec swing with full depletion. All steps are tube-furnace and plasma steps.
why: Atomically thin, trap-free channel shrinks GIDL and trap leakage and is vertically stackable (facts 2-3).

title: Image-sensor pixels as memory: pinned-photodiode storage cells
idea: Reverse the image sensor: in existing 55-90 nm CMOS image sensor fabs, use a light-shielded pinned photodiode as the storage well, the transfer gate as the access device, and the floating diffusion plus source follower as an in-cell gain readout, with write-back through a reset/inject path. Pinned photodiodes show dark currents of ~1-10 e-/s, so a few-thousand-electron packet holds for minutes.
why: Near refresh-free retention (fact 3) on idle trailing-node CIS capacity; density ~1-3 Mb/mm2 limits it to a retention tier, while charge transfer in tens of ns stays DRAM-class.

title: Image-sensor foundry dark pixels as long-retention memory cells
idea: CMOS image sensors fight exactly DRAM's leakage physics (SRH generation) and win: pinned photodiodes reach dark currents of ~1-10 electrons/s (~1e-18 A), against DRAM's 13 fA tail. Tape out a $200-300k MPW in a CIS process with light-shielded 4T pixels repurposed as memory. The pinned diode stores ~5,000 electrons written by fill-and-spill through the transfer gate, the transfer gate is the access device, and the floating diffusion with source follower gives a gain readout.
why: ~1e4x lower leakage means minutes of retention at room temperature. The tapeout is a cheap testbed for pinned-storage-node physics in future DRAM cells and a refresh-free macro for U.S. CIS lines (fact 3, U.S. manufacturability).

title: Image-sensor pinned-photodiode storage: hold the bit like a dark pixel
idea: Scale and time shift from CMOS image sensors, whose pinned photodiodes hold charge 10-100 ms at ~1 e-/s dark current: store each bit as a charge packet in a fully depleted buried n-well capped by a p+ pinning layer, moved by a transfer gate onto a floating-diffusion gain node for sensing, so the pinned surface removes the interface generation that dominates DRAM leakage.
why: Leakage (fact 3): ~1 e-/s versus the DRAM tail of ~8e4 e-/s means minutes of retention with only ~1-2k electrons stored, also relaxing the capacitor charge wall (fact 1); Si, B, P only.

title: Implant-free Schottky source/drain access devices from flexible electronics
idea: Flexible electronics cannot use high-temperature implant anneals, so they rely on Schottky metal contacts. Build the DRAM access transistor with silicide Schottky source and drain (no junction implants, no activation anneal), accepting its higher thermionic off-leakage and a 1% raw BER from the weakest cells.
why: Facts 2 and 4: drops implant and anneal steps and allows low-temperature access devices in stacked 3D tiers, easing a 3D DRAM blocker; refresh at the 1% quantile keeps refresh near today's level.

title: Assembly-line takt sweep: every row restored by normal reads
idea: Set the memory controller's address mapping and scheduler so streaming workloads (LLM weight sweeps, frame buffers) activate every row within a takt time below tREFW. Disable refresh and verify coverage with a per-row activation bitmap.
why: Zero refresh power: restore happens as a free side effect of reads that occur anyway. Fits HBM in inference, where weights are swept every token.

title: Refresh-off KV-cache zones with recompute-on-ECC-fail
idea: Po: memory that forgets on purpose. LLM serving runtimes tag KV-cache and activation pages as decay-tolerant; the controller places those banks in a ~1 s refresh mode, and when on-die ECC flags an uncorrectable block the runtime recomputes that token's keys and values from the prompt instead of faulting.
why: Fact 3: KV cache is often 30-60% of inference DRAM; cutting its refresh 16x removes most refresh energy there and returns bandwidth to compute.

title: Canary-cell event-driven refresh replaces the fixed clock
idea: Time shift from clock-driven (fixed 64 ms) to event-driven refresh: each subarray carries a row of deliberately weakened canary cells (smaller capacitor, slightly lower Vt) whose leakage tracks 2x the true array tail; a comparator watches them and the bank refreshes only when a canary crosses threshold, automatically tracking temperature, voltage and aging.
why: Refresh energy (fact 3): removes the 4-8x worst-case guardband baked into fixed intervals; at 45 C refresh ops fall ~4x.

title: Negative-capacitance gate stack sharpens the access transistor's off-switch
idea: Reverse the sign of capacitance: add a thin ferroelectric layer tuned for negative-capacitance operation in series with the access transistor's gate oxide, so the internal gate voltage amplifies the wordline swing and subthreshold slope drops below 60 mV/dec. Vt can then be raised ~150 mV for leakage with no loss of on-current and no higher wordline voltage.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3) ~10x lower at equal Ion, relaxing refresh; or equal leakage at ~0.5 V lower wordline, easing the voltage floor (fact 10).

title: Stainless-steel foil substrate doubles as global back gate and heatsink
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: make the substrate do three jobs. Oxide or 2D thin-film access transistors are built on a dielectric-coated stainless-steel foil; the foil itself is a static global back gate biased negative to push every array transistor into deep off-state, while also spreading heat and shielding the array (periphery lives on a separate die).
why: Deep off-state without per-row negative wordline pumps (Facts 3, 7, 10); roll-to-roll foil processing cuts capital per bit and uses abundant U.S. steel.

title: Pneumatized bird-bone air-gap spacers isolate wordlines from storage nodes
idea: Bird bones are hollowed by air sacs; in vertical-channel BEOL DRAM, fill the gaps between adjacent wordlines and storage-node contacts with sacrificial polynorbornene that decomposes at 350-400 C through a porous cap, leaving sealed air gaps (k=1).
why: Cuts wordline-to-node coupling ~3x, so the passing-gate row-hammer threshold rises ~3-5x and neighbor-field GIDL falls; wordline capacitance and CV2 drop ~30%.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory pods run DRAM at 77 K, refresh off
idea: Effect: Arrhenius freeze-out of generation and subthreshold leakage. DIMMs/HBM sit on closed-loop LN2 cold plates; at 77 K subthreshold slope is ~15-20 mV/dec and generation ~exp(-Eg/2kT) collapses, so retention exceeds hours, refresh is disabled and Vt/VDD are retuned for cold operation.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth to ~0 (fact 3), wire resistance ~6x lower (fact 5), lower VDD (fact 10); cooling cost amortized at rack scale.

title: Solar-cell field-effect passivation transplanted onto storage-node sidewalls
idea: Scale jump from square-metre solar cells to 15 nm cell pillars: line the isolation sidewalls where the storage junction's depletion region meets the surface with ALD Al2O3 carrying ~-5e12 cm^-2 fixed charge (the PERC passivation trick), keeping the p-well surface accumulated so surface SRH generation, a major junction-leakage source, shuts off.
why: Junction leakage/refresh (fact 3): solar passivation lowers surface recombination ~100x; at DRAM pitch where surface-to-volume is huge, expect 2-5x lower junction leakage with Al and O only.

title: Substitute static cell plate with idle-lowered plate voltage
idea: Substitute the constant cell-plate voltage with one that drops ~0.2-0.3 V while a bank is idle. That couples every floating storage node down and shrinks the storage-to-gate field that drives GIDL on '1' cells; the plate returns before activation, and the negative wordline tracks it to keep '0' cells off.
why: GIDL-dominated tail leakage drops ~3-5x, lengthening the self-refresh interval accordingly; a circuit-only change needing no gas-consuming process step.

title: Park bitlines at VDD during self-refresh to zero ones' drain bias
idea: TRIZ #9 Preliminary anti-action: remove the harmful driving force before it acts. During long idle and self-refresh, bitlines are parked at VDD instead of VDD/2, so the vulnerable charged '1' cells see zero drain-source voltage and essentially no subthreshold loss, while '0' cells, protected by the negative wordline and far from their sense threshold, absorb the larger bias.
why: Removes the subthreshold component of the retention tail in standby (Fact 3): ~2-3x longer self-refresh interval for idle phones and servers at zero area cost.

title: Built-in negative-charge dielectric replaces negative wordline pumps
idea: TRIZ #8 Anti-weight: counterbalance the depletion-mode tendency of wide-gap oxide TFTs with permanent charge. An AlOx layer on the glass substrate, carrying its native fixed negative charge (~1e12-1e13 cm-2, the effect used for solar-cell field passivation), sits under each channel as a static counterweight that shifts Vt positive by ~1 V, so the off-state is deep at a 0 V wordline.
why: Removes negative-wordline charge pumps and their periphery area and energy (Facts 7, 10) while keeping deep off-state leakage (Fact 3).

title: Solar MPPT perturb-and-observe loop tunes each bank's negative wordline
idea: Solar inverters find the maximum-power point by nudging voltage and watching the response. Off-state leakage versus negative wordline voltage has a minimum (subthreshold falls while GIDL rises), so an on-die loop nudges each bank's VNWL by +/-25 mV, reads a replica-transistor leakage integrator, and settles at that bank's minimum for its current temperature and age.
why: Fixed VNWL is set for worst-case corners; tracking the true minimum could cut tail leakage 2-3x across temperature and aging (fact 3) for negligible area.

title: Ratchet ferroelectric gate that locks Vt high after every access
idea: Random stimulus 'ratchet wrench': it turns freely one way, then locks. A thin HZO layer in the access gate stack is pulsed to low-Vt polarization at wordline rise, and a short negative tail pulse at wordline fall ratchets it back to a +0.5 V high-Vt state, so retention-state isolation needs no standing negative wordline bias.
why: Decouples on-current from off-leakage (fact 3) and removes negative-wordline pumps from the periphery (fact 7); leakage tail down ~1000x. Risk: needs ~1e15 minor-loop cycles versus HZO's ~1e11-1e12 today.

title: Built-in electret charge in gate stack replaces negative wordline
idea: Worse: run a negative-wordline charge pump all through standby to hold Vt up. Flip: embed a fixed negative charge layer (Al2O3/SiO2 interface dipole or implanted electret) on the storage-node side of the access gate so the device carries a built-in +Vt shift only where leakage matters.
why: Removes negative-wordline pump energy and area (facts 3, 7) and cuts GIDL at the storage node.

title: Mechanic's torque wrench: per-row fused negative wordline level
idea: A mechanic torques each bolt to its own spec. At test, each row's leakiest cell is measured and a 3-bit fuse sets that row's off-level from 0 to -0.6 V, applied by its local sub-wordline drivers; strong rows sit near 0 V (low GIDL, low stress) and only weak rows get deep negative bias.
why: A single global negative wordline trades subthreshold leakage against GIDL; tuning per row lifts worst-case retention ~2-4x and reduces the large wordline swings that aggravate row hammer.

title: Laser-trimmed wordline-low voltage per subarray at its leakage minimum
idea: Like laser-trimming thin-film resistors to spec, measure each subarray's leakage vs negative-wordline voltage at wafer test. Fuse-trim each subarray's VNWL and body bias to the bottom of its own V-shaped curve, the balance of subthreshold against GIDL.
why: The optimum wordline-low shifts by a few hundred mV across a die. Per-subarray trimming could cut tail leakage 2-5x at almost no area.

title: Only 10 nm may change: wide-gap Si:C pocket against GIDL
idea: Limit: the channel stays silicon, and only the 10 nm under the gate-drain overlap may be altered. Selectively grow a carbon-alloyed Si1-yCy or 3C-SiC pocket at the storage-side drain edge. Its wider local bandgap exponentially suppresses band-to-band GIDL tunneling where the negative wordline meets the high storage node.
why: Facts 3 and 10: BTBT current scales roughly as exp(-Eg^1.5/F). Widening the local gap by 0.2-0.3 eV could cut GIDL ~10-30x and allow a deeper negative off-voltage without a GIDL penalty.

title: Set-top-box firmware updates: on-die microcoded refresh sequencer
idea: Adapted from over-the-air firmware updates: replace the hard-wired refresh counter with a tiny on-die microcontroller running signed microcode (refresh ordering, multi-rate bins, temperature curves, row-hammer mitigations), updatable by the host through a mode-register channel for the module's whole life.
why: Refresh and row-hammer policy can be repaired after deployment as new leakage behavior or attacks appear (facts 3, 9), instead of replacing hardware, keeping modules in service longer.

title: Nacre brick-and-mortar nanosheet gate dielectric for BEOL access FETs
idea: Nacre's aragonite tiles in organic mortar stop cracks from running straight through; stack exfoliated perovskite nanosheets (Ca2Nb3O10, k ~200, 1.5 nm) at room temperature by Langmuir-Blodgett, staggered like bricks, with sub-nm Al2O3 'mortar' by ALD at 150 C, so no straight grain-boundary leakage path crosses the gate dielectric.
why: Gives EOT <0.5 nm with low gate leakage at <=150 C, so low-temperature oxide channels get near-ideal gate control (~65 mV/dec); Vt can rise and the off-current tail drops ~10-100x.

title: Mousetrap NbO2 threshold switch in series with storage contact
idea: Random stimulus 'mousetrap': nothing happens until the trigger passes a threshold, then it snaps. Insert a thin NbO2 threshold-switching layer in the storage-node contact; in retention the tiny voltage across it keeps it insulating as a second, non-MOS leakage barrier, while the ~VARY/2 seen during access snaps it conductive in nanoseconds.
why: Stacks a leakage blocker with different physics under the MOS tail, so the two tails do not coincide (fact 3). Risk: NbO2 sub-threshold leakage and threshold variation must stay well below fA, and the read signal must survive the snap.

title: High-voltage cable stress-grading spacer that defuses the GIDL hotspot
idea: Adapted from stress-grading sleeves at HV cable terminations, which use high or field-dependent permittivity to spread equipotentials at the shield cut: form the gate-drain spacer of the buried-wordline device from a graded-k stack (high-k at the gate corner fading to low-k toward the storage node). The field at the overlap corner is spread over a longer distance instead of peaking.
why: The gate-edge corner is where GIDL and trap-assisted tunneling concentrate; grading the field there could cut the leakage tail about 10x (fact 3) and permit a deeper negative wordline for lower subthreshold leakage.

title: Magnify the dielectric's job: linear high-k by day, ferroelectric at shutdown
idea: Make the DRAM capacitor dielectric a ZrO2/HfZrO2 morphotropic blend that acts as a k~50 linear dielectric under normal +/-0.5 V operation, and only when a power-loss detector fires a 2.5 V plate pulse is stored charge converted into remanent polarization; a power-up pulse converts it back.
why: DRAM-class endurance during operation plus survival of power loss; ferroelectric fatigue spent only once per power cycle; higher k also helps Cs (fact 1).

title: Share the accelerator cold-plate loop with HBM and DIMMs
idea: Extend the GPU liquid-cooling cold plates over HBM stacks and DIMMs to hold the arrays at 30-40 C instead of 85-95 C. Thermal sensors then step the refresh multiplier down from 2x to 0.25x.
why: Retention roughly doubles per 10 C, so 16-20x more retention headroom. The 10-20% refresh bandwidth loss falls below 1% and refresh energy drops ~90%.

title: Refresh-free transient zones for AI KV-cache and activations
idea: Box: standard DRAM/HBM x standard access x standard sense x controller tags rows as transient with a write timestamp x system x Si x firmware. Accelerator runtimes guarantee activation and KV-cache blocks are rewritten or freed within 32 ms, so the controller skips refresh on rows written within tRET and on freed rows.
why: Much of HBM holds data younger than tRET; skipping its refresh recovers 10-20% bandwidth and refresh power (fact 3) on the scarcest memory.

title: Buy retention-reject dies and run them in fast-refresh CXL pools
idea: Box: commodity dies that failed 64 ms retention x standard access x standard sense x CXL expander controller with 8-16 ms refresh and per-row remap x system x Si x zero masks. A company buys downgraded dies at scrap prices, profiles them, and sells pooled CXL capacity where extra refresh is hidden by bank parallelism.
why: Raises usable supply by reclaiming a few % of output now scrapped or downgraded, with zero fab capital (capital intensity, supply).

title: JEDEC retention-map register and per-row refresh command
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x standard sense x vendor-measured retention class per row group exposed in a readable register plus a targeted-row refresh command x controller multi-rate refresh x Si x zero masks. Policy: push the standard through JEDEC and require it in CHIPS-funded and federal procurement so every vendor ships it.
why: Most rows retain >1 s; multi-rate refresh cuts refresh 70%+ (fact 3) but has been blocked by missing vendor data, which a standard unlocks.

title: Substitute sputtered IGZO with N2-curtain spatial-ALD gallium-tin oxide
idea: Substitute argon/oxygen-sputtered IGZO with amorphous Ga-Sn-O deposited by atmospheric-pressure spatial ALD, in which nitrogen gas curtains rather than argon separate the precursor zones. The result is an indium-free wide-gap channel with angstrom thickness control at high throughput.
why: Indium-free oxide-semiconductor access devices (~1e-19 A/um off-current class) made without rare gases or vacuum tools: a cheaper BEOL tier for refresh-light gain cells.

title: Stamped snap-dome nanobeam stores bits as buckled up or down
idea: Like keyboard snap domes stamped from prestressed sheet, each cell is a prestressed nanobeam buckled up or down, flipped electrostatically in ns and read capacitively. Contact-free flexing avoids wear.
why: Zero refresh: the bit is mechanical shape, not charge, so nothing leaks. Zero standby and refresh power, with GHz-resonator-class flexures able to reach high endurance.

title: Let out-of-the-money options expire: recomputable data receives no refresh
idea: Traders let options expire when exercising costs more than they are worth. Tag regions holding recomputable data (KV-cache blocks rebuildable from tokens, cached embeddings, prefetch buffers) as 'expire-allowed': they get long or no refresh, ECC flags any decayed line, and the runtime recomputes it on demand.
why: KV caches are a growing share of inference DRAM; dropping their refresh and accepting rare recompute saves refresh power and lets weaker-retention, cheaper dies serve them (fact 3, cost per bit).

title: Firefighters' bucket brigade: CCD charge transfer replaces long bitlines
idea: A bucket brigade passes water hand to hand instead of filling a long pipe. Cells line a buried-channel CCD column; on access, the selected cell dumps its packet into the CCD, low-swing three-phase clocks walk it ~32 stages to a floating-diffusion sense node at the mat edge, and it is walked back to rewrite, so no long bitline is ever charged.
why: Only the signal packet (~10k electrons) moves, at low clock swing, instead of a ~50-100 fF bitline per bit, cutting array energy per access ~10x; revives 1970s CCD memory with modern image-sensor transfer efficiency (>99.999%).

title: Millisecond flash-lamp anneal gives crystalline, low-trap stacks on cheap glass
idea: TRIZ #21 Skipping (rushing through): heat only the top micrometres to ~900-1000 C for ~1 ms with xenon flash lamps, so the gate dielectric densifies and the oxide channel crystallises while the soda-lime glass or polymer substrate stays below its softening point.
why: Lower interface and bulk trap density cuts trap-assisted leakage and VRT (Fact 3) without costly quartz or sapphire substrates; flash-lamp tools are low capex (Fact 4).

title: Millisecond flash anneal grows rutile TiO2 capacitor without ruthenium
idea: Time shift in processing: replace the Ru/RuO2 template normally needed for high-k rutile TiO2 with a ~1 ms flash-lamp or laser anneal that drives as-deposited Al-doped TiO2 on TiN through the anatase-to-rutile transition before the TiN oxidizes, yielding k~80-100.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1) feeding retention (fact 3): ~2x Cs at the same aspect ratio doubles retention (halves refresh) or lets AR drop ~2x; removes Ru and Hf dependence.

title: Adiabatic resonant charging for refresh wordlines and bitline restore
idea: Fuse adiabatic logic with refresh bursts. A stepwise or LC-resonant supply ramps the 3 V wordlines and restore drivers, and charge from the row being closed is recycled into the next row opened.
why: Recovers 50-70% of refresh CV^2 energy, roughly 46 to 20 fJ/bit (facts 3 and 10).

title: Leakage-keeper latch: make the leaks hold the bit, stacked vertically
idea: Inverts 'leakage destroys stored data': build a loadless 4-device latch where the access devices' OFF leakage is engineered ~10x larger than the cross-coupled drivers' leakage, so leakage itself replenishes the high node and the cell is static with no refresh. Stack the four devices in two BEOL tiers (n-type and p-type oxide channels) over CMOS so the footprint approaches a 1T1C cell.
why: Zero refresh energy and bandwidth loss (fact 3) and no capacitor (fact 1) at ~6-8F2 footprint via vertical stacking; standby power drops to ~fA per bit.

title: SF6 breakers to vacuum interrupters: nano vacuum-gap access switch
idea: The grid is replacing SF6 gas-insulated breakers with vacuum interrupters because vacuum insulates without fluorinated gas. Build a lateral 20-30 nm vacuum-gap field-emission switch, sealed by a PVD cap, whose emitter tip conducts only when the wordline gate thins the barrier; off-state current is Fowler-Nordheim limited and there is no substrate junction.
why: Removes junction and subthreshold leakage paths entirely (fact 3) with temperature-insensitive retention, and the cavity seal needs no fluorinated chemistry.

title: UNSW light-steered hydrogenation re-passivates deep access-transistor traps
idea: UNSW's 'advanced hydrogenation' for solar cells shines intense light during a 200-400 C anneal to set hydrogen's charge state (H0/H-), letting it diffuse far and bond to otherwise unreachable defects. Apply a flash-lamp or LED-illuminated hydrogenation step after capacitor formation so hydrogen reaches buried-wordline gate-oxide and channel traps hidden under the capacitor stack.
why: Interface traps under the buried gate drive GIDL and trap-assisted tunneling in the tail (fact 3); deeper, charge-state-controlled passivation could halve Dit and shrink tail leakage 2-5x.

title: Silicon-on-nothing: each storage junction floats over a sealed void
idea: Scale shift from MEMS cavities to the single cell: use the silicon-only empty-space-in-silicon process (trench array plus high-temperature H2 anneal so Si surface-migrates into a sealed buried void) to put a vacuum void directly under each storage-node junction, removing bottom junction area and blocking substrate minority-carrier diffusion.
why: Junction leakage (fact 3): bottom-area and diffusion terms are often >50% of junction leakage, so ~2-4x retention gain with only Si and H2.

title: Self-aligned dipole layer raises threshold only near storage node
idea: Box: standard cap x buried-channel access with an Al2O3 dipole interlayer added after a partial wordline recess x SA x in-array x Si x recess-deposit-etchback on existing patterns (zero masks). The dipole shifts local Vt ~+0.3 V only in the upper gate segment beside the storage junction, while the lower channel keeps low Vt for drive.
why: Higher off-state barrier exactly where leakage originates: ~10x lower subthreshold/GIDL leakage (fact 3) without drive loss.

title: Graphene's roll-to-roll CVD line repurposed for MoS2 access channels
idea: Graphene transistors failed as switches because graphene has no bandgap, yet roll-to-roll CVD growth and transfer of graphene worked. Reuse those R2R furnaces and transfer lines to grow monolayer MoS2 (1.8 eV gap) on metal foil and laminate it onto capacitor foils as the access channel.
why: An atomically thin, wide-gap access channel: off-current approaches 1e-18 A/um with good electrostatics at short channels. R2R processing cuts capital per square meter.

title: Zipper NEMS contact closes at one volt, opens to air
idea: Random stimulus 'zipper': it closes progressively from one end with little force. A curved nano-cantilever contact anchored at the bitline zips onto the storage-node pad under a ~1 V wordline because the electrostatic gap at the zipping front is tiny; released, it springs back to a 10 nm gap, with Ru/RuO2 contact faces and a hermetic cavity to fight stiction.
why: A physical gap has no subthreshold or junction leakage, so refresh nearly vanishes, and low actuation voltage attacks the 3 V wordline floor (facts 3, 10). Risk: 1e15-cycle contact endurance.

title: Soap-bubble air-gap spacers made by dry polymer decomposition
idea: Random stimulus 'soap bubble': a film that vanishes and leaves only air. Place a sacrificial polynorbornene spacer between the buried-wordline cap and the storage-node contact; after sealing under a porous cap, a 400 C anneal decomposes it to gas, leaving a k=1 air gap with no wet release and no rinse.
why: The air gap cuts wordline-to-node fringing field (lower GIDL, fact 3) and coupling (row hammer, fact 9); dry decomposition replaces the wet spacer strip/rinse loop (>10x less water for that step).

title: Trim each leaky access transistor once, like programming flash
idea: Inverts 'the leakage tail is frozen at fab-out': add a thin nitride trap layer in the access-transistor gate stack; at wafer test retention-profile every cell and apply a one-time hot-carrier program pulse only to the ~0.1% tail cells, raising their Vt by 150-300 mV so their OFF current falls 10-100x. A BIST mode re-trims in the field as cells age.
why: Removes the tail that sets the refresh interval (fact 3): 64 ms -> >=512 ms across the die, ~8x lower refresh energy and bandwidth tax for one extra deposition.

title: GaN/AlN tunnel-diode pair self-holds the bit without refresh
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: let the cell maintain itself. On GaN-on-sapphire, two room-temperature GaN/AlN resonant tunnelling diodes are stacked in series with the storage node at their midpoint; their negative-differential-resistance curves intersect at two stable points, so the node self-restores against leakage at pA standby current, accessed through one GaN HEMT.
why: Refresh eliminated (Fact 3) with non-destructive hold; risk is RTD peak-to-valley ratio and standby current per bit (needs <10 pA/bit for 1 Gb under 10 mW).

title: Threshold-graded tiers selected by voltage eliminate the staircase
idea: IFR: select a tier with no staircase contact. Within each 8-tier group, every tier's channel is deposited with a composition giving a Vt step of ~0.4 V; one vertical wordline selects tier k by amplitude, reads by differential sensing between steps k and k-1, and writes top-down in a cascade so lower-Vt tiers rewritten later are not disturbed.
why: Constraint: staircases and tier contacts are a major area and cost item in 3D memory; removing them makes added tiers nearly free, a key lever for 10x bits at constant wafer cost.

title: Manhattan Project parallel paths for a refresh-free access device
idea: Revive the Manhattan Project's parallel uranium-enrichment strategy: fund four competing access-device routes (SiC, vacuum nano-gap, NEM relay, zinc oxide) at four U.S. sites against one fixed spec (>=10 s retention at 85 C, <=30 ns access, >=1e16 cycles), with shared test vehicles and a hard down-select at 18 months.
why: De-risks the physics of fact 3 in parallel and shortens time to a solution, concentrating domestic capital on the access device, the biggest refresh lever.

title: Substitute fixed sense reference with co-decaying reference cells
idea: Substitute the static VDD/2 bitline reference with reference cells in each row, written to half charge whenever the row is written. They leak through identical access transistors, so the sense threshold sags with the '1' cells instead of staying fixed.
why: Sense margin decays more slowly: 2-3x longer refresh interval for ~1% array area, with refresh energy and bandwidth loss cut proportionally.

title: Negative-capacitance HZO gate raises access threshold without drive loss
idea: Box: standard pillar cap x recessed-channel access with an HZO negative-capacitance layer over the gate oxide x standard SA x in-array x Si x ALD gate-stack swap. NC voltage amplification gives sub-60 mV/dec swing, so Vt can be raised ~200 mV at the same on-current.
why: ~100x lower subthreshold leakage at equal drive (fact 3), 4-10x less refresh, or same leakage at lower wordline voltage (fact 10).

title: Eliminate refresh of read-only copies: re-fetch from durable backing store
idea: Read-only data (weights, embeddings) is mapped to never-refreshed banks with strong per-line ECC; when ECC flags drift the line is re-fetched from a NAND or CXL pool that holds the master copy, and a scrubber rewrites lines nearing their measured retention age. Refresh becomes on-demand repair.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth fall to near zero for the read-only majority of inference memory, trading rare microsecond re-fetches for constant refresh.

title: Self-referenced slow sensing during refresh rescues decayed cells
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x SA run in two-step self-reference only during refresh (read and hold bitline level, write a known 1, read again, compare) x in-mat x Si x zero masks. Comparing the cell with itself removes capacitor and offset mismatch, so cells decayed to ~25% of signal still resolve; normal reads stay fast.
why: Refresh need only catch cells before ~75% decay instead of ~50%, allowing ~2x longer intervals (fact 3); the extra latency hides in background refresh.

title: Compact free memory into refresh-off segments
idea: Reverse the OS goal from spreading pages to packing them: a kernel compaction daemon migrates live pages out of the top DRAM segments whenever utilization falls, then switches those segments' refresh off using partial-array self-refresh or segment masking that LPDDR5/DDR5 already support.
why: Servers average ~40-60% DRAM utilization and phones idle with free memory; refresh-off empty segments cut refresh/idle power ~30-50% (fact 3); software only.

title: SEU-style bit interleaving turns clustered weak rows into random errors
idea: Rad-hard memories interleave codeword bits across distant cells so one particle strike flips at most one bit per word. Spread each codeword over the chips and subarrays that are activated together, so a weak row, a VRT cluster, a bad access-transistor column or a hammered row adds at most one bit per codeword, keeping errors iid at the 1% cell BER the code is sized for.
why: Facts 3 and 9: a cheap code handles 1% raw BER without being beaten by correlated failures, and row-hammer flips are absorbed without per-row counters, saving periphery area.

title: Leaky-integrate-and-fire timestamps let sense references track decay
idea: Neurons integrate with a known membrane time constant; store a 3-4 bit coarse refresh timestamp per row in a sidecar column, and have the sense-amp reference DAC slide with elapsed time to follow the expected droop of '1's and creep of '0's, so a half-decayed cell still resolves.
why: Tracking margin over time stretches usable retention ~1.5-2.5x, cutting refresh rate ~50%.

title: Tin-catalyzed bottom-up nanowire access transistors grown in place
idea: Sn: place Sn catalyst dots on storage-node landing pads with a relaxed DUV pattern, shrink them to ~10-15 nm by controlled dewetting, then grow vertical Si nanowires by Sn-catalyzed vapor-liquid-solid growth below 400 C, switching in-situ doping to form source, channel and drain, followed by an ALD gate-all-around.
why: Single-crystal gate-all-around access devices at sub-litho diameter without EUV (fact 4), at a thermal budget low enough to sit above capacitors in 3D stacks (fact 2).

title: Venusian alien's diamond access transistors for hot, chiller-free memory
idea: An alien from 460 C Venus would never cool its memory. Grow boron-delta-doped or hydrogen-terminated diamond (5.5 eV gap) thin-film access FETs by low-temperature plasma CVD over the capacitors; leakage stays sub-fA even at 150-200 C, so DRAM can sit hot beside accelerators.
why: Today refresh doubles every ~10 C, which forces cooling; diamond access devices hold retention at 150 C, cutting refresh to near zero and removing memory-side chiller energy, and diamond needs only carbon.

title: Access transistor nested inside the capacitor's hollow pillar
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: use the hollow core of the tall cylinder capacitor as the body of a vertical access transistor. An ALD channel lines the upper inner wall and a gate electrode fills the core, so the device gets a 150-300 nm channel length (killing DIBL and short-channel subthreshold leakage) without using any lateral area.
why: Breaks the 'smaller cell vs. longer, less leaky channel' contradiction (Facts 2, 3): ~10x lower subthreshold leakage and a route to 4F2 without a separate transistor tier.

title: Fluorinated alumina electret plane gives every access transistor built-in back bias
idea: F: bury a fluorine-implanted Al2O3 layer under the active area; Al2O3:F holds a stable negative fixed charge (~5e12 cm^-2) that acts as a permanent negative body bias, raising Vt and suppressing subthreshold leakage without a pumped VBB rail or heavy channel doping.
why: Deletes the body-bias charge pump from the periphery (fact 7) and lowers the channel doping that sharpens junction fields and GIDL (fact 3); ~2-3x lower leakage at equal on-current.

title: Plasmodesmata junctionless access channels need no dopant activation
idea: Plant cells connect through continuous plasmodesmata channels that callose closes by squeezing; build the access device as a junctionless, uniformly n-doped 3-5 nm channel (in-situ doped In2O3 or poly-Ge:P deposited at 350 C) that a wrap gate fully depletes to turn off.
why: With no p-n junctions there is no >900 C activation anneal and no junction GIDL or trap-assisted junction leakage, often the dominant tail component, so tail leakage drops ~10x within 400 C.

title: Building inspector's occupancy certificate: per-bank retention data in SPD
idea: An inspector certifies each room's safe occupancy. A JEDEC rule, seeded by CHIPS Act procurement, requires every module's SPD to store measured per-bank retention at three temperatures from final test, and DRAM to expose per-bank refresh-rate registers, so the OS and controller refresh each bank at its own rate instead of the global worst case.
why: Most banks retain 4-16x longer than the worst bank; standardized data unlocks ~2-4x refresh savings across the installed base with firmware, not fabs.

title: Supercritical CO2 deuterium passivation at 250C, no masks
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x SA x whole-wafer post-BEOL treatment x Si x supercritical CO2 carrying D2/D2O at ~250C and >100 bar. The supercritical fluid penetrates dense metal stacks to reach junction and gate-oxide traps that forming-gas anneals miss, and Si-D bonds resist thermal/hot-carrier depassivation better than Si-H.
why: Shrinks and stabilizes the tail, including variable retention time (fact 3), with zero masks on cheap US-buildable tools.

title: Power-MOSFET superjunction pillars inside the vertical access transistor
idea: Adapted from the superjunction in high-voltage power MOSFETs: build the vertical-channel access device with alternating thin p and n columns, charge-balanced so they fully deplete sideways. This flattens the electric-field peak at the drain/storage-node edge where band-to-band tunneling (GIDL) originates.
why: GIDL rises exponentially with peak field; a 30-40% lower peak could cut tail leakage 10-100x (fact 3) without a thicker oxide or longer channel, keeping the 4F2 vertical-channel footprint.

title: Tea-bag vapor monolayer doping grades the storage junction
idea: Random stimulus 'tea bag': steep it gently and the dose is set by contact. Dose the storage-node side of the vertical channel with a self-limiting vapor-phase phosphorus-precursor monolayer, cap it in situ and flash-anneal; one dry cycle gives a conformal, deliberately graded, low-peak junction on every pillar face.
why: Replaces angled implants, their resist strips and wet cleans (>10x less water for the junction loop), and the graded profile lowers the peak field that drives GIDL and trap-assisted tunneling: tail leakage 3-5x lower (fact 3).

title: Substitute silicon channel with beta-Ga2O3 ultrawide-gap access transistor
idea: Substitute the crystalline-Si access channel with a 4-6 nm beta-Ga2O3 (Eg 4.8 eV) gate-all-around channel built as a tier over the CMOS periphery and crystallized by local anneal. Its intrinsic carrier density is ~1e-22 that of Si, and because it contains no indium it avoids the indium supply that IGZO depends on.
why: Leakage tail/refresh: off-current below 1e-20 A per cell stretches retention from 64 ms to >100 s, cutting refresh energy and bandwidth loss by >99%. It goes beyond the IGZO prior work with a wider gap and no indium.

title: Replace amorphous oxide liners with epitaxial CaF2 crystalline insulator
idea: Substitute the amorphous SiO2/SiN gate insulator and isolation liner around the access channel with epitaxial CaF2 (0.6% lattice mismatch to Si) grown by MBE on Si {111} facets. A crystalline insulator has orders of magnitude fewer border traps than an amorphous oxide.
why: Variable retention time (VRT) and random telegraph noise come from border and oxide traps; removing them shrinks the retention tail so refresh is set by the bulk distribution: 2-4x longer tREF.

title: Substitute silicon channel with sulfurized MoS2 grown in H2S/N2
idea: Substitute Si with a bilayer MoS2 access channel made by ALD of MoO3 and conversion in H2S/N2 at ~600 C in a resistive furnace (no argon carrier), then encapsulated in thermal-ALD Al2O3. The ~1.3 nm body has no dangling-bond surface generation sites and near-ideal electrostatics.
why: The atomically thin body and 1.6-1.8 eV gap suppress subthreshold and short-channel tunneling leakage: target <1 aA per cell, with gate length down to ~5 nm for 3D stacking.

title: TFET gatekeeper fused in series with a MOSFET access channel
idea: One wordline gates a single channel with a p+ tunnel-junction segment next to the storage node and a conventional n+ MOSFET segment toward the bitline. In the off state the band-to-band tunnel junction blocks with a steep (<40 mV/dec) turn-off, and in the on state the MOSFET segment supplies the drive current.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): about 100x lower off-current at the same on-current. The refresh interval goes from 64 ms to seconds, cutting refresh energy by ~90%.

title: Wafer-scale monolayer WSe2 on sapphire: junction-free atomically thin switch
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells and thin films: use a 0.7 nm monolayer channel grown by MOCVD directly on c-plane sapphire and double-gated so the gate controls every atom of the channel; with no bulk, no pn junction and a ~1.6-2 eV gap, junction generation leakage vanishes and short-channel leakage stays suppressed at ~10 nm gate length.
why: A small, low-leakage access device (Facts 2, 3) on a non-silicon, crucible-free substrate; risks are contact resistance and defect-assisted leakage.

title: Series lock gate: second gate per channel shared by subarray
idea: Box: cap x vertical channel with two stacked gates (row wordline + a subarray-wide lock gate nearest the storage node) x SA x in-array 3D x Si x second gate tier deposited in the same trench. The lock gate stays deeply negative except when its subarray is active, adding a series stack that multiplies isolation.
why: Stack effect plus deeper off-bias cuts leakage 10-100x in idle subarrays (most of the chip), extending their refresh (fact 3) and blocking hammer coupling into them (fact 9).

title: 2050 engineer's hBN-sealed WSe2 access channel with vdW contacts
idea: A 2050 engineer would wonder why we ever used channels with dangling bonds. Transfer a monolayer WSe2 or MoS2 channel, fully encapsulated top and bottom in hBN, onto the capacitor tops and contact it with van der Waals-transferred metal, so there are no doped junctions or pinning defects; leakage is bounded by the 1.6-2 eV gap and atomically clean interfaces.
why: Removes the junction/trap-assisted-tunneling tail behind the 13 fA spec (fact 3); projected off-current <1e-19 A per cell gives seconds-to-minutes retention, and a 0.7 nm body suppresses DIBL so channels can shorten (density).

title: Dam engineer's spillway: resonant-tunneling barriers isolate the storage node
idea: A dam spillway passes water only above a set level. Replace the access channel with a double-barrier quantum-well stack (AlN/GaN/AlN or SiO2/Si-well/SiO2) between bitline and storage node; the wordline shifts the well's subband into resonance for fast transfer, while off-resonance transmission through two barriers is exponentially suppressed.
why: On/off ratios of 1e15 or more with no doped junction remove refresh, and transfer happens at ~1 V; extends the UltraRAM barrier idea to DRAM speed and endurance.

title: Dangling-bond-free 2D channel removes interface-trap leakage tail
idea: Po: the channel has no surface. Wrap a WSe2 or MoS2 monolayer channel around the pillar with an hBN gate dielectric so there are no dangling bonds at the channel interface, leaving the trap-assisted tunneling that creates the leakage tail and variable retention time with no sites to act through.
why: Fact 3: the tail and VRT are trap-driven; a trap-free channel could tighten the off-current distribution ~100x and extend refresh interval ~10x.

title: Epitaxial CaF2 gate insulator removes the traps behind VRT
idea: Ca: grow crystalline CaF2 (12 eV gap, within 0.6% lattice match to Si(111)) as the access-transistor gate insulator by fluoride epitaxy; its ionic, dangling-bond-free interface removes the border and interface traps whose capture/emission causes variable retention time and random-telegraph leakage.
why: VRT cells force pessimistic refresh guard-bands (fact 3); a trap-free insulator could shrink the VRT population ~10x and allow ~2x longer refresh.

title: Lawnmower-pattern weight streaming makes inference itself the refresh
idea: Random stimulus 'lawnmower': one planned pass covers the whole lawn. The inference runtime lays out weights so every token's weight sweep visits every HBM row in the refresh counter's order within tREFW; because activation restores the row, the base die verifies the sweep and suppresses explicit refresh for every row it covered.
why: LLM decoding reads all weights every ~20-50 ms, so explicit refresh can drop >90%; refresh energy and its embedded generation and cooling water fall >10x for inference HBM (fact 3).

title: Arrhenius leakage odometer schedules refresh by integrated charge loss
idea: Leakage scales as exp(-Ea/kT), so integrate a per-module charge-loss budget, the integral of exp(-Ea/kT(t)) dt, from DIMM thermal-sensor samples. Measure each module's Ea at boot by timing first failures at two temperatures. Refresh when the integral reaches the equivalent of 64 ms at 85 C. Controller firmware plus validation costs well under $1M and 12 months.
why: With Ea ~0.6 eV, a DIMM at 50 C leaks ~8x less, and at 40 C ~16x less, than in the 85 C case the spec assumes. Refresh energy and bandwidth fall 5-10x in typical fleets (fact 3).

title: Molybdenum roasting loop: tungsten-free, recoverable dual-work-function wordline
idea: Adapted from the molybdenum industry's purification route (roast to MoO3, which sublimes near 700 C and recondenses pure): make the buried wordline and contacts from Mo with a lower-work-function cap near the storage junction to cut GIDL, so the only refractory metal on the die is one that end-of-life roasting recovers cleanly.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) from the access device, lowers GIDL through the dual work function (fact 3), and gives scrap dies a simple metal-recovery route; Mo is mined in the U.S.

title: Purdue SiC DRAM revived by the EV silicon-carbide wafer glut
idea: Purdue's 1990s 4H-SiC DRAM cells held charge for years at room temperature, because the 3.26 eV gap suppresses thermal generation, but the work stalled on expensive, defect-ridden SiC wafers. EV power electronics have since made 200 mm SiC cheap. Build a planar 1T1C SiC cell with a nitrided gate oxide on U.S.-grown SiC, using spare power-device line capacity, as a refresh-free DRAM-class tier.
why: Near-nonvolatile DRAM that needs essentially no refresh, made on existing U.S. SiC capacity. Density is lower than silicon DRAM, so the gains are energy per bit and supply security, not cost per bit.

title: Monolayer 2D channels shrink the lateral access device to 5 nm
idea: IFR: the lateral transistor takes up no length. Use a 0.7 nm MoS2 or WSe2 monolayer channel in each 3D tier (low-temperature MOCVD or transfer); its atomic thinness suppresses short-channel leakage so gate length drops to ~5 nm and the tier cell footprint shrinks ~3x.
why: Constraint: fact 2's lateral-transistor blocker shrinks, cutting break-even tiers from ~26 to ~9, so ~30 tiers give ~10x density at similar wafer cost.

title: Satellite data-carousel memory: detect, then refetch the golden copy
idea: Broadcast satellites loop data so receivers fill gaps. Treat DRAM as a 1%-BER cache of data that also lives in NAND or CXL far memory: each 4 KB block has a CRC plus a light code that fixes most errors, uncorrectable blocks are refetched from the golden copy, and DRAM refreshes only at its 1% age.
why: Fact 3: for read-mostly data (weights, page cache, embeddings, roughly half of server DRAM) refresh falls ~10x and parity stays ~3-5%, since rare failures cost a refetch, not a stronger code.

title: Nanosolar's aluminum foil anodized into capacitor pores with diode floors
idea: Nanosolar's roll-to-roll CIGS on aluminium foil died on efficiency, but its cheap Al-foil web still works. Anodize the foil roll into self-ordered alumina pores at 100 nm pitch and 60:1 aspect ratio, and line them by ALD as MIM capacitors. Stepping down the anodization voltage at the end thins each pore floor's barrier layer to ~2 nm (about 1.2 nm per volt), forming a self-aligned MIIM tunnel diode as each cell's access element.
why: Attacks the capacitor wall with high-aspect-ratio pores that need no etch tool, plus an electrochemically defined access barrier. Aluminium is abundant (no tungsten) and the process is roll-to-roll.

title: Retention-reject die salvage with per-row refresh controller cards
idea: A die that fails a 64 ms retention screen usually fails because of a few hundred rows, not the whole die. Buy retention-downbinned DRAM at scrap prices and profile every row at 85 C on ~$50k FPGA testers. Sell CXL or DIMM cards whose controller refreshes the weak ~0.1% of rows at 16 ms and the rest at 64 ms. $1M covers testers, the controller FPGA image and first inventory within 24 months.
why: Adds usable bits from existing fabs at near-zero capital, recovering perhaps 1-3% of output that is scrapped or sold into low-grade markets today (supply, capital intensity, fact 3).

title: Quantum-confined 3 nm silicon body widens the bandgap without new materials
idea: Confining silicon to a ~3 nm body raises its subband edges, so the effective gap grows ~0.2-0.3 eV. Because n_i ~ exp(-Eg/2kT), generation drops by about exp(-0.25/0.052), roughly 100x. Build the vertical access channel as an ultrathin crystalline silicon shell on a dielectric core (macaroni-style as in 3D NAND, crystallized by laser or lateral solid-phase epitaxy), so the whole depletion region around the storage node is confined.
why: This gives ~100x less thermal generation in silicon itself (fact 3) and fits existing deposition and anneal tools and vertical 3D cell concepts (fact 2).
